purpose: Resolve the most substantial numeric planning-distance contradictions using source-defined reaches, not replacement distances inferred from endpoint separation.

cases.decision: Access-review hold; preserve the original lower-reach record for correction.
cases.finding: The catalog combines a 6.9-mile lower-reach feature sequence with the NYSDEC Route 3 fishing access, about 16.7 straight-line miles from its DeGrasse finish. The source's lower-reach State Put-in is described on Tooley Pond Road, 5.9 road miles southeast of DeGrasse. The Route 3 access identifies a different, much longer start with intervening carries.

sources.review: Search-indexed primary reach description inspected: Lower South Branch, 6.9 miles, Class IV-V, Tooley Pond Road start and DeGrasse bridge boundary. Direct fetch returned 403; current access operations were not verified from this historical description.

Current DEC page distinguishes the Route 3 fishing access at 44.2481,-74.7836, upstream hand-launch context and named carries from Spruce Mountain and First Brook accesses. A parking coordinate does not establish a wet entry or the shorter AW reach.
DEC identifies the downstream forest access setting; this is not proof that the catalog's entire upstream-to-downstream combination is the documented 6.9-mile run.

cases.releaseRequires: Verify the actual lower-reach start and DeGrasse water entry/boundary, match the complete feature and carry sequence, confirm lawful current access, correct every dependent record and inspect regenerated geometry. Do not silently move the put-in to an approximate nearby parking site.

cases.decision: Access-review hold on this connector; retain the separately bounded adjacent guides.
cases.finding: A six-mile guide joins Site 5 Route 28 Overlook north of Poland to Site 9 North Middleville, about 11.3 straight-line miles apart. The March 2020 operator study's Figure 2-1 places Newport Dam between these sites; section 3.3.1 identifies a portage in the broader Dover Road-Middleville section. The catalog claims high confidence without resolving that transfer.

sources.review: Complete relevant pages visually inspected: PDF page 9 / printed page 5, Figure 2-1; PDF page 23 / printed page 19, section 3.3.1. The map identifies Sites 5, 7, Newport Dam, Site 8 and Site 9 in order. This historical study does not establish present dam conditions, portage availability or public wet entries.

cases.releaseRequires: Resolve the current Newport site and lawful take-out/carry/relaunch, confirm exact endpoints and measured itinerary, revise time and distance from that evidence, and inspect separate paddle-leg geometry. Do not infer uninterrupted passage or use straight-line distance as river mileage.

cases.decision: Access-review hold pending independent confirmation of the full Todd connection.
cases.finding: The seven-mile, three-hour estimate is repeated from a conditions website, while the stored endpoints are about 14 straight-line miles apart. The official park map documents 12.5 miles from Elk Shoals to Wagoner alone (2 + 5.5 + 5 miles), shows hazards requiring carries, and does not cover the full Todd connection. Neither the estimate nor its implied continuous itinerary is established.

sources.review: The page currently repeats seven miles and about three hours, alongside estimated flow guidance. Its local note also describes a gauge take-out, so it does not independently resolve the named park itinerary.

Full one-page August 2023 map visually inspected, including the canoe-distance table, south-to-north flow note and hazard/portage symbols. Do not add its downstream segment times into an unverified full Todd trip or treat old mapped carries as present permission.
Current park page identifies Wagoner and Elk Shoals as separate access areas. Facility availability does not validate the seven-mile Todd itinerary.
Current county inventory names Todd Island Park separately from Todd River Access. Access-site listings alone do not establish the intervening trip length or passage.

cases.releaseRequires: Verify the exact Todd and Wagoner water entries, independent full-route mileage and time, all intervening carries/hazards and lawful current access. Keep numeric profiles and the Jefferson gauge as research context until separately reviewed.

hubIdentityCorrection.finding: Hub names came from the first route sorted by reach; API names could instead follow score order. Four public families were labeled as only one branch despite retaining main-river records.
hubIdentityCorrection.rule: If branch/fork records coexist with an existing route name whose normalized identity exactly matches the family ID, use that family name. Otherwise retain the existing fallback; do not invent a name from the slug or merge new families.
hubIdentityCorrection.preserved: Every individual reach name, river ID, route order, scoring profile, gauge assignment, access coordinate, hazard and canonical path. The alias-only Allen/Allens Creek case remains unchanged.

hubDistanceCorrection.finding: The static hub template treated every number in a distance label as miles, while the API read the first number. Road numbers, access numbers, mileposts and contextual figures polluted the displayed bounds. West Canada Creek showed 3-28 mi because of Route 28; St. Regis reached 458 mi because of Route 458.
hubDistanceCorrection.change: Use one server-side parser for static and API hub summaries. Read the first explicit mileage expression, including its numeric range, and reject road/time-only labels. Preserve hundredth-mile precision for short trips.
hubDistanceCorrection.scope: Numeric static summary bounds change on 38 of 382 indexable hubs; no hub becomes unquantified. This changes summaries, not stored trip mileage, geometry, distance filters or source validity.
hubDistanceCorrection.limits: A label parser cannot verify river length or fully resolve compound itineraries, alternate take-outs or contextual source disagreements. The remaining source-review queue is still required; guide-specific totals should ultimately be represented as reviewed structured data.
